title: 1 Kings Chapter 17 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Kings chapter 17 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Kings Chapter 17 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Kings Chapter 17.

questions.question: Who was Elijah described as in 1 Kings 17:1?
questions.correctAnswer: A Tishbite from Gilead
questions.explanation: Elijah is described as 'the Tishbite, who was of the inhabitants of Gilead' in 1 Kings 17:1.

questions.question: What did Elijah declare to King Ahab about the weather in 1 Kings 17:1?
options: There shall not be dew nor rain these years
Only dew will fall but no rain
There shall be snow instead of rain
questions.correctAnswer: There shall not be dew nor rain these years
questions.explanation: Elijah declared to Ahab that 'there shall not be dew nor rain these years' as stated in 1 Kings 17:1.

questions.question: Where was Elijah commanded to hide according to 1 Kings 17:3?
options: By the brook Cherith, before Jordan
questions.correctAnswer: By the brook Cherith, before Jordan
questions.explanation: God commanded Elijah to hide by the brook Cherith, which is before Jordan, as per 1 Kings 17:3.

questions.question: What was Elijah told he would drink from while at the brook Cherith?
questions.correctAnswer: Water from the brook
questions.explanation: Elijah was told he would drink from the brook Cherith, meaning water from the brook, in 1 Kings 17:4.

questions.question: Who was commanded to feed Elijah while he stayed by the brook Cherith?
questions.correctAnswer: The ravens
questions.explanation: God commanded the ravens to feed Elijah there, as stated in 1 Kings 17:4.

questions.question: How often did the ravens bring food to Elijah?
questions.correctAnswer: In the morning and evening
questions.explanation: The ravens brought bread and flesh to Elijah both in the morning and in the evening, according to 1 Kings 17:6.

questions.question: What happened to the brook Cherith after a while?
questions.correctAnswer: It dried up
questions.explanation: The brook dried up because there was no rain in the land, as told in 1 Kings 17:7.

questions.question: True or False: Elijah was instructed to go westward after the brook Cherith dried up.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Elijah was instructed to go to Zarephath, which is eastward and belongs to Zidon, as per 1 Kings 17:9.

questions.question: True or False: Elijah drank from the brook Cherith while the ravens fed him bread and flesh.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Elijah drank of the brook and the ravens brought him bread and flesh, as stated in 1 Kings 17:6.

questions.question: What command did the LORD give Elijah in 1 Kings 17:3?
questions.correctAnswer: Hide by the brook Cherith
questions.explanation: The LORD told Elijah to 'hide thyself by the brook Cherith,' according to 1 Kings 17:3.

questions.question: Which event occurred first in 1 Kings 17?
options: Elijah dwelt by the brook Cherith
Elijah declared no rain would fall
questions.correctAnswer: Elijah declared no rain would fall
questions.explanation: Elijah first declared the drought in 1 Kings 17:1 before dwelling by the brook Cherith or other events.

questions.question: True or False: The word of the LORD came to Elijah after the brook Cherith dried up.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The word of the LORD came to Elijah after the brook dried up, as stated in 1 Kings 17:8.

questions.question: What did Elijah do when he arrived at the brook Cherith?
questions.correctAnswer: Dwelt by the brook Cherith
questions.explanation: Elijah went and dwelt by the brook Cherith as commanded by the LORD, according to 1 Kings 17:5.

questions.question: According to 1 Kings 17:4, who commanded the ravens to feed Elijah?
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD
questions.explanation: The LORD commanded the ravens to feed Elijah, as stated in 1 Kings 17:4.

questions.question: True or False: Elijah stood before the LORD God of Israel when he spoke to Ahab.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Elijah said to Ahab, 'before whom I stand,' referring to the LORD God of Israel, in 1 Kings 17:1.

medium.title: 1 Kings Chapter 17 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Kings Chapter 17 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What command did the LORD give Elijah regarding where to go after the brook Cherith dried up?
options: Go to Zarephath and stay with a widow who will provide for you
Return to Ahab and prophesy a drought
Go to Jerusalem and seek the priests
Stay by the brook and wait for the rain
questions.correctAnswer: Go to Zarephath and stay with a widow who will provide for you
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 17:9 commands Elijah to arise and go to Zarephath, where a widow has been commanded by God to sustain him. This follows the drying up of the brook as stated in verses 7-8.

questions.question: What was the widow woman doing when Elijah first met her at the gate of Zarephath?
questions.correctAnswer: Gathering sticks
questions.explanation: According to 1 Kings 17:10, the widow woman was gathering sticks when Elijah called to her at the city gate. This sets the context for the request Elijah made.

questions.question: What did Elijah ask the widow woman to bring him first?
questions.correctAnswer: A morsel of bread
questions.explanation: Elijah first asked the widow to bring him a morsel of bread as recorded in 1 Kings 17:11, even before she fetched water in the previous verse.

questions.question: How did the widow describe her food supplies when Elijah asked for bread?
options: A handful of meal in a barrel and a little oil in a cruse
Several loaves stored in the house
A large amount of grain and oil
questions.correctAnswer: A handful of meal in a barrel and a little oil in a cruse
questions.explanation: In 1 Kings 17:12, the widow explained she only had a handful of meal in a barrel and a little oil in a cruse, enough to make food for her and her son before they die.

questions.question: What did Elijah tell the widow to do despite her scarcity of food?
options: Make a little cake for him first, then for herself and her son
Save all the food for her son
Leave the city and seek help
Store the meal and oil for later
questions.correctAnswer: Make a little cake for him first, then for herself and her son
questions.explanation: Elijah encouraged her not to fear and to make a little cake for him first, then for herself and her son as shown in 1 Kings 17:13. This demonstrates trust and obedience.

questions.question: What promise did Elijah give the widow about her meal and oil if she obeyed him?
options: The barrel of meal will not waste nor the cruse of oil fail until the LORD sends rain
She will become wealthy beyond measure
She will be protected from famine
Her son will be healed immediately
questions.correctAnswer: The barrel of meal will not waste nor the cruse of oil fail until the LORD sends rain
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 17:14 records Elijah's promise that the barrel of meal would not waste and the cruse of oil would not fail until the day the LORD sends rain upon the earth, showing God's provision.

questions.question: What was the result when the widow obeyed Elijah's instructions about making bread?
options: She, Elijah, and her household ate for many days
The meal and oil spoiled quickly
questions.correctAnswer: She, Elijah, and her household ate for many days
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 17:15 states that the widow, Elijah, and her household ate many days as a result of her obedience, confirming God's provision through faith and action.

questions.question: How does 1 Kings 17:16 illustrate God's faithfulness through Elijah's prophecy?
options: The barrel of meal did not waste and the cruse of oil did not fail
Elijah was fed by ravens again
questions.correctAnswer: The barrel of meal did not waste and the cruse of oil did not fail
questions.explanation: Verse 16 confirms the fulfillment of Elijah's prophecy as the barrel of meal and cruse of oil remained sufficient, demonstrating God's faithfulness to His promises.

questions.question: What does the interaction between Elijah and the widow teach about faith and obedience?
options: Obedience to God's word results in provision even in scarcity
Faith is unnecessary when resources are available
One should rely solely on personal strength
questions.correctAnswer: Obedience to God's word results in provision even in scarcity
questions.explanation: The passage from 1 Kings 17:12-16 shows the widow's obedience despite scarcity, leading to God's provision, teaching the importance of faith and obedience.

questions.question: According to 1 Kings 17:13-14, what was Elijah’s attitude toward the widow’s fear and scarcity?
options: He told her not to fear and to trust God's provision
He scolded her for lack of faith
He left her to suffer without help
He advised her to leave the city
questions.correctAnswer: He told her not to fear and to trust God's provision
questions.explanation: In verse 13, Elijah tells the widow 'Fear not' and assures her of God’s provision in verse 14, emphasizing trust over fear.

questions.question: What can a believer learn from the widow’s willingness to share her last food with Elijah?
options: Generosity and faith in God’s promise bring blessings
Self-preservation is more important than sharing
Only the wealthy should give to others
questions.correctAnswer: Generosity and faith in God’s promise bring blessings
questions.explanation: The widow’s act of sharing her last meal as instructed by Elijah (1 Kings 17:12-15) shows that generosity coupled with faith leads to God’s blessing.

questions.question: What does 1 Kings 17:15-16 teach about God's provision during times of famine?
options: God provides continually for those who obey Him
Provision is based on human effort alone
Famine cannot be overcome by faith
questions.correctAnswer: God provides continually for those who obey Him
questions.explanation: These verses demonstrate that despite famine, God provided for Elijah and the widow's household as they obeyed His word, highlighting divine faithfulness.

questions.question: True or False: Elijah told the widow to prepare food for herself and her son before making any for him.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 17:13 shows Elijah instructing the widow to make a little cake for him first, then for herself and her son, reversing the natural order out of faith.

questions.question: True or False: The widow initially felt hopeless and expected to die due to lack of food.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: In 1 Kings 17:12, the widow expresses that she and her son expected to eat their last meal and die, showing her despair before Elijah’s promise.

questions.question: True or False: The widow’s obedience to Elijah’s words resulted in her household being fed for many days.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 17:15 records that the widow, Elijah, and her household ate many days after she obeyed Elijah’s instructions, demonstrating God’s provision through obedience.

hard.title: 1 Kings Chapter 17 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Kings Chapter 17.

questions.question: What was the condition of the widow's son when he fell sick according to 1 Kings 17?
options: He had no breath left in him
questions.correctAnswer: He had no breath left in him
questions.explanation: The verse states that the widow's son's sickness was so severe that there was no breath left in him, indicating death or near death (1 Kings 17:17).

questions.question: How did the widow initially react to Elijah's presence after her son became sick?
options: She questioned if he came to remind her of her sin and kill her son
She asked him to pray for her son immediately
questions.correctAnswer: She questioned if he came to remind her of her sin and kill her son
questions.explanation: The widow said to Elijah, 'What have I to do with thee, O thou man of God? art thou come unto me to call my sin to remembrance, and to slay my son?' (1 Kings 17:18), showing her suspicion and distress.

questions.question: Where did Elijah take the widow's son after asking for him?
options: Into a loft where he laid him on his own bed
questions.correctAnswer: Into a loft where he laid him on his own bed
questions.explanation: Elijah took the child out of the woman's bosom, carried him up into a loft, and laid him upon his own bed as recorded in 1 Kings 17:19.

questions.question: What was Elijah's prayer to God regarding the widow's son?
options: That the child would be healed gradually
That the child's soul would come into him again
That the child would be taken to heaven
That the widow would gain more faith
questions.correctAnswer: That the child's soul would come into him again
questions.explanation: Elijah prayed, 'O LORD my God, I pray thee, let this child's soul come into him again' (1 Kings 17:21), petitioning God to restore the child's life.

questions.question: What was the result of Elijah's prayer for the widow's son?
options: The soul of the child came into him again and he revived
The child was healed but remained weak
questions.correctAnswer: The soul of the child came into him again and he revived
questions.explanation: The LORD heard Elijah's voice, and the soul of the child came into him again, causing him to revive (1 Kings 17:22).

questions.question: What did Elijah do after the child was revived?
options: He prayed again for full recovery
He brought the child down to the house and gave him to his mother
He placed the child at the city gate
questions.correctAnswer: He brought the child down to the house and gave him to his mother
questions.explanation: Elijah took the child and brought him down out of the chamber into the house and delivered him unto his mother (1 Kings 17:23).

questions.question: How did the widow respond to the miracle of her son’s revival?
options: She acknowledged Elijah as a man of God and the truth of the LORD's word
She asked Elijah to stay with her
questions.correctAnswer: She acknowledged Elijah as a man of God and the truth of the LORD's word
questions.explanation: The woman said, 'Now by this I know that thou art a man of God, and that the word of the LORD in thy mouth is truth' (1 Kings 17:24).

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in the narrative of Elijah reviving the widow's son by laying himself upon the child three times?
questions.correctAnswer: Repetition for emphasis
questions.explanation: Elijah stretched himself upon the child three times (1 Kings 17:21), showing repetition as a literary device to emphasize the earnestness of his prayer and action.

questions.question: The miracle of reviving the widow's son prefigures which New Testament event?
options: Jesus raising Lazarus from the dead
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus raising Lazarus from the dead
questions.explanation: Elijah raising the widow's son prefigures Jesus raising Lazarus (John 11:43-44), both demonstrating God's power over death (1 Kings 17:22).

questions.question: Which other Old Testament prophet also performed a resurrection miracle similar to Elijah’s in 1 Kings 17?
questions.correctAnswer: Elisha
questions.explanation: Elisha, Elijah’s successor, also raised the Shunammite’s son from death (2 Kings 4:32-35), echoing the miracle in 1 Kings 17:22.

questions.question: What is the significance of the Hebrew word translated as 'soul' in Elijah's prayer for the widow's son?
options: It indicates only the breath of life
It means the entire being or life force
It refers exclusively to the spirit after death
It is a term for the body
questions.correctAnswer: It means the entire being or life force
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'nephesh' translated as 'soul' in 1 Kings 17:21 connotes the whole living person or life force, not just breath or spirit alone.

questions.question: How does Elijah's dependence on God for sustenance by the brook Cherith contrast with the widow's initial scarcity in Zarephath?
options: Elijah was fed miraculously while the widow faced famine
Elijah had food but no water, the widow had water but no food
questions.correctAnswer: Elijah was fed miraculously while the widow faced famine
questions.explanation: Elijah was fed by ravens at brook Cherith (1 Kings 17:6), but the widow had only a handful of meal and a little oil, fearing death by famine (1 Kings 17:12).

questions.question: Which theme from 1 Kings 17 is echoed in Jesus’ teaching in Matthew 6 regarding provision?
options: Faith in God’s provision despite scarcity
questions.correctAnswer: Faith in God’s provision despite scarcity
questions.explanation: Elijah and the widow’s story in 1 Kings 17 shows God’s provision in scarcity, paralleling Jesus’ teaching to trust God for daily needs in Matthew 6:25-34.

questions.question: True or False: Elijah's prayer for the widow's son was immediately answered after he stretched himself upon the child three times.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 17:21-22 records that after Elijah prayed and stretched himself upon the child three times, the LORD heard his prayer and the child revived.

questions.question: True or False: The widow initially believed Elijah would help her son without any doubt.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The widow questioned Elijah's intent, suspecting he came to remind her of sin and to slay her son (1 Kings 17:18), indicating doubt and fear.

theological.title: 1 Kings Chapter 17 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Kings Chapter 17 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What divine attribute is demonstrated by God's command to Elijah to be fed by ravens at the brook Cherith?
questions.correctAnswer: God's omnipotent provision
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 17:4-6 shows God commanding ravens to bring food to Elijah, demonstrating His sovereign power to provide supernaturally for His prophet in a desolate place, a clear display of divine provision.

questions.question: According to 1 Kings 17:1, what was the purpose of Elijah's declaration of no dew or rain upon the land?
options: To demonstrate the LORD's control over nature
To encourage people to worship Baal
questions.correctAnswer: To demonstrate the LORD's control over nature
questions.explanation: Verse 1 shows Elijah declaring a drought 'before whom I stand,' emphasizing God's sovereign authority over natural elements, underscoring His supremacy over Baal, who was falsely worshiped as a rain god.

questions.question: How does the widow’s experience in Zarephath (verses 12-16) illustrate the doctrine of God's sustaining grace in hardship?
options: God provides abundantly even with limited human resources
God requires human effort without divine aid
God punishes the faithful for their sins
God's grace is only for the Israelites
questions.correctAnswer: God provides abundantly even with limited human resources
questions.explanation: In verses 12-16, the widow has only a handful of meal and little oil, yet God miraculously ensures they do not run out. This reveals God’s sustaining grace that supplies needs beyond natural limitations.

questions.question: What theological significance can be drawn from Elijah’s prayer for the widow’s son and the child's resurrection (verses 20-22)?
options: God responds to faithful intercession with life-giving power
Death is irreversible regardless of prayer
Elijah acts independently of God's will
questions.correctAnswer: God responds to faithful intercession with life-giving power
questions.explanation: Verses 20-22 reveal that Elijah’s prayer results in the restoration of the child's life, showing God’s power over death and His responsiveness to the prayers of His servants, foreshadowing Christ’s resurrection power.

questions.question: The command to Elijah to hide by the brook Cherith (verse 3) primarily demonstrates which aspect of God's providence?
questions.correctAnswer: God’s protective guidance
questions.explanation: In 1 Kings 17:3, God directs Elijah to a specific hiding place where he will be safe and cared for, illustrating God's providential protection over His servants during times of crisis.

questions.question: What combined doctrine is taught by Elijah’s proclamation of drought (verse 1) and God’s provision through the widow (verses 9-16)?
options: God’s sovereign judgment and merciful provision
Human effort is the source of provision
God’s judgment is cruel without mercy
Nature is independent of God’s will
questions.correctAnswer: God’s sovereign judgment and merciful provision
questions.explanation: Verse 1 shows God’s judgment by withholding rain, while verses 9-16 show God’s merciful provision for Elijah through the widow, teaching that God’s sovereignty encompasses both judgment and grace.

questions.question: How does the widow's response to Elijah in verse 18 reflect a theological understanding of suffering and sin?
options: She associates her son's death with divine punishment for sin
She fully trusts God’s goodness without question
She expects Elijah to perform magic
questions.correctAnswer: She associates her son's death with divine punishment for sin
questions.explanation: In verse 18, the widow questions if Elijah has come to remind her of her sin which might have caused her son's death, reflecting the common theological belief that suffering can be a consequence of sin.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is most clearly revealed by the promise that the barrel of meal and cruse of oil will not fail until the rain returns (verse 14)?
questions.correctAnswer: God’s faithfulness to His promises
questions.explanation: Verse 14 presents God's promise that resources will not run out, demonstrating His steadfast faithfulness to fulfill His word and sustain His people even in drought.

questions.question: What does Elijah’s act of stretching himself upon the child three times (verse 21) symbolize in a typological sense related to Christ’s redemptive work?
options: Christ’s repeated intercession and resurrection power
questions.correctAnswer: Christ’s repeated intercession and resurrection power
questions.explanation: Elijah’s repeated laying on of the child and prayer in verse 21 typologically prefigures Christ’s intercession for humanity and His power over death through resurrection.

questions.question: How does 1 Kings 17:24 contribute to the apologetic defense of Elijah’s prophetic authority?
options: It shows a firsthand witness affirming the truth of Elijah’s word
It reveals Elijah’s failure to perform miracles
It denies the validity of Elijah’s prophecy
It emphasizes human wisdom over divine revelation
questions.correctAnswer: It shows a firsthand witness affirming the truth of Elijah’s word
questions.explanation: Verse 24 records the widow's confession that Elijah is a true man of God because the word of the LORD in his mouth is truth, providing eyewitness testimony that supports Elijah’s prophetic authority.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that miracles in 1 Kings 17 are mere folklore with no divine origin. What does 1 Kings 17:20-22 actually teach about the nature of true miracles?
options: True miracles are acts of God responding to faithful prayer, evidenced by the resurrection of the widow’s son
Miracles are human inventions to control people
Miracles can be explained scientifically without God
questions.correctAnswer: True miracles are acts of God responding to faithful prayer, evidenced by the resurrection of the widow’s son
questions.explanation: Verses 20-22 describe God answering Elijah’s prayer by restoring life to the widow’s son, affirming that biblical miracles are divine acts confirming God's power and presence, not folklore.

questions.question: What theological insight emerges from combining Elijah’s initial declaration of drought (verse 1) and the later restoration of the widow’s son (verse 22)?
options: God’s sovereign control includes both judgment and restoration
questions.correctAnswer: God’s sovereign control includes both judgment and restoration
questions.explanation: Verse 1 shows God’s judgment through drought, and verse 22 shows God’s power to restore life, together teaching that God’s sovereignty governs both punishment and redemption.

questions.question: What narrative arc connection does 1 Kings 17 demonstrate in relation to Israel's covenant relationship with God?
options: God’s faithfulness to His covenant promises despite Israel’s sin
God’s silence in times of crisis
questions.correctAnswer: God’s faithfulness to His covenant promises despite Israel’s sin
questions.explanation: The chapter shows God judging Israel with drought yet sustaining Elijah and the widow, signaling that God remains faithful to covenant promises and provides grace amidst judgment.

questions.question: What doctrine is taught by God commanding Elijah to arise and go to Zarephath where a widow will sustain him (verse 9)?
options: God’s providential care extends beyond Israel to Gentiles
God’s blessings are limited to priests only
God’s care is only for the wealthy
God abandons His servants in foreign lands
questions.correctAnswer: God’s providential care extends beyond Israel to Gentiles
questions.explanation: Verse 9 directs Elijah to Zarephath, in Sidon, a Gentile region, where God commands a widow to sustain him, illustrating God's providential care reaching beyond Israel to foreigners.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is revealed by Elijah’s cry to the LORD asking if evil has been brought upon the widow by slaying her son (verse 20)?
options: God’s justice and sovereignty over suffering
God’s weakness in responding to prayer
questions.correctAnswer: God’s justice and sovereignty over suffering
questions.explanation: In verse 20, Elijah appeals to God's justice and sovereignty, acknowledging God's control over suffering and questioning the reason for the child's death, highlighting God's righteous governance.
